Use case: historical-scene. Generate ONE original high-definition photorealistic cinematic landscape frame in a FIVE-SCENE SET of ordinary domestic life in the SAME imagined late-fifteenth-century BHUYAN VILLAGE in Assam. This is an artistic period interpretation using the project's comparative references, not authenticated historic house plans or dated costume evidence. Input settlement reference establishes low ordinary bamboo-and-timber houses with pale earth-infill walls, thick complete straw roofs, modest raised timber floors or low earthen plinths, plain wooden posts, timber stairs, simple doors and shutters with NO glass, domestic woven screens, areca and banana trees, small pond, paths and fenced household yards. Scenes should feature COMMON HOMES, not the large chiefly residence or previous Ahom royal carved-palace aesthetic. No ornate palace columns, gold furniture, royal jewellery, navy guards, modern houses, tiled/metal roof, concrete, glass window, electricity, plastic, vehicles, tourists or signs. Women's clothing must follow the supplied comparisons: simple white/cream blouses, long white/cream wrapped lower garments with narrow muted red/green/ochre woven borders, broad white shoulder cloth sometimes loosely drawn over the head, modest small earrings/necklace/bangles; different natural ages and faces, not copied stock-photo poses or cloned identities. Sankardev, ONLY where the shot requests him, must match his ONE character design from the supplied sheet: clean-shaven youthful/mature oval face, strong dark arched brows, large dark eyes, neck-to-shoulder length black hair swept back, plain unbleached white dhoti and white upper drape with very narrow ochre border on LEFT shoulder, RIGHT shoulder/arm bare, barefoot, no turban/crown/beard/jewels/halo/staff. A turnaround sheet depicts one person many times; NEVER duplicate him into multiple panel figures. Faces, eyes, hands, woven fabric and household objects must be crisp, clearly readable and naturally lit at close/medium camera distance; good focus, natural skin pores and realistic anatomy, no distant indistinct people or plastic skin. Preserve warm natural daylight and a restrained cream/earth-brown/bamboo-green palette, realistic household scale, calm documentary atmosphere. When a sanchi-pat manuscript appears, it is a horizontal bundle of elongated rectangular tan/brown processed BARK FOLIOS with fine dark handwritten ink rows, slightly irregular fibrous edges, separate wooden cover boards and cloth wrap nearby; not a modern bound printed book, not white paper, not a scroll and not an open Bible. Any visible script is small and incidental, no invented prominent readable quotations. A THOGA is a low wooden manuscript book-rest on the floor, with a broad rectangular flat or mildly inclined support board carried by simple carved low wooden supports, sized for the long folios; no tall church lectern or modern desk. The thoga and folios must be fully visible when requested, not hidden behind hands or decorative cloth. No text overlays, captions, panel borders, collage, watermark, copied stock logo or studio backdrop. One coherent landscape frame, 16:9, ideally 2560x1440; prioritise clear faces and artefact details.
